cells.tense: You're tending what's growing, and you're doing it with your own hands on the work.
cells.ask: Offer one finished thing to someone who'd honor it — let the completion be seen, and let that settle you.
cells.core:
What you've been cultivating gets its care without force from you. You water it when it needs water, you leave it alone when it needs that, and the shape holds. There's a steadiness in how you work right now — hands in the soil, no rushing, no panic about whether it'll come up. You know what this thing is for and you're giving it exactly what it needs.

That ease is what this place looks like when you're tuned to it. You're aimed at something real, not a fantasy, and the tending and the aim are working together instead of pulling against each other. One thing you've finished is ready to be handed over or set down. Let it be seen as done, not still in progress. What fills in behind it isn't applause — it's the plain rest of work completed, and enough left in you to start the next row.
cells.sheetLine: You tend what's growing, and it's growing.
cells.verb: Tending what grows, by hand, through form.
cells.place: The pull toward light you can recognize but never manufacture — the thing you steer by.

cells.tense: You're already caring for a harvest that hasn't come in yet, braced for a yield you can't see.
cells.ask: Treat one thing you've already imagined well enough as real, and spend the day as if it's on its way.
cells.core:
You're living a season ahead — already tending demands that haven't arrived, already watering what might not sprout — and the caretaking has gotten ahead of the growth. You're pulling the shoot up to check the roots. When you do that, the plant dies. Every conversation turns into a rehearsal for something that hasn't happened, and the thing you're actually tending gets none of you.

What this place looks like when it's held right is care that doesn't exhaust, holding without clutching. That's already yours to pick back up. The vision isn't the problem — you've imagined this thing thoroughly enough to trust it. Stop working a field that isn't planted yet. Spend today inside the one you've actually built, and let the satisfaction be real now instead of later.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending a harvest that isn't in yet.
cells.verb: Tending what grows, by hand, through form.

cells.tense: You used to have your hands in what mattered, and you're still standing at the edge of the work you stepped away from.
cells.ask: Do one small tending act today — not because you feel like it, but because the light's still up there and you know where it is.
cells.core:
The pull is still there. You can point at the light from here, name what it is — and your hands are off the work. What you used to tend has kept growing or it hasn't, and either way you're watching from outside the fence. The recognition didn't go anywhere. The tending did.

What this place looks like when it's held right is care without force, holding without clutching. You hadn't lost that. You just stopped showing up. Keep hoping and keep doing — one small thing today, a bit of care you don't feel like giving — and the current starts moving back through you. Not for the outcome. For the hands being in it again.
cells.sheetLine: You set the work down and haven't picked it back up.
cells.verb: Tending what grows, by hand, through form.
cells.place: The pull toward light you can recognize but never manufacture — the thing you steer by.

cells.tense: You're tending things right now — this room, these people, this outcome — and calling it just what happens.
cells.ask: Say out loud once what you've been doing, to one person, and let them tell you they see it.
cells.core:
The care is running — you're shaping what happens around you every day, adjusting, tending, keeping things viable — and when anyone asks, you say it's nothing, just logistics, just what needed doing. The tending is real. The one doing it hasn't claimed the doing. You'd credit the circumstances before you'd credit your own hands.

What this place looks like when it's held right is care that doesn't exhaust, holding without clutching. Nothing new is required to get there. It asks that you say the thing once, to one person who can hear it, and let it be witnessed. Not because it was hidden. Because it was yours and nobody said so, including you.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending it now and calling it nothing.
